Musée National de la Marine, Toulon

LocationPlace Monsenergue, Quai de Norfolk, 83000 Toulon, France
Visited14 September 2016
WebsiteMusée National de la Marine de Toulon

Museum Report

The Musée National de la Marine operates branches in Brest, Port-Louis, Paris, Rochefort and Toulon. The Toulon branch museum is located adjacent to the Naval Base in Toulon, within walking distance of the CBD.

The centre piece of the museum two huge models, a sailing frigate and a ship of the line, which are mounted on gimbals so they could sit an entire class in front of them and demonstrate how the ships would react to given conditions and controls or test the class by setting some and asking "What would you do now?" If you spin the models around, the other side is cut away to show the internals.

The most significant modern artefact in the museum is the machinery control console from the post-war aircraft carrier Clemenceau.

They also have a good collection of models of 20th century warships, including a quite large model of the modern carrier Charles de Gaulle.

Toulon is a nice location in a very scenic part of the world, and was my favourite town on the French Riviera. While the museum is probably oriented more towards the sailing navy than my personal area of interest, it is certainly worth going to if you are in the area.

p.s. I am indebted to ChrisPat from the NavWeaps forum for some of the details in this report.
